analysis: Integration pass over the SSD hybrid checkpoint expiry-classification change. Code change: provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift splits removeCorrupt into a private removeFile(tag) that does the same performIndexedRemoval (ownsEvictionRoot check under removalLock, removeItemIfSafe under root, index.remove) plus a separate corruptDropped increment. In scanOnDisk (head ~lines 155-165), the TTL check is moved from the validation guard into its own guard. A file past its TTL is now unlinked through removeFile and skipped with `continue` before index.insert and the commitments update, so it is never indexed. Files that fail header, metadata, weightHash, layoutEpoch, blockSize or lookupTag-prefix checks still go through removeCorrupt. The 30-minute TTL bound (T-041 mitigation b) remains enforced at scan time, and expired ciphertext is still deleted. No change to DBK3 crypto, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, epoch handling (the epoch is not rotated by either path, matching the T-041 detection_hint), disk budget, or storage validation. The docs and changelog match the code. Tests add an expiry case that asserts corruptDropped == 0 and a corruption case that asserts it equals 1, which preserves the corruption signal. Residual items, none a regression: removeFile can silently skip deletion when ownsEvictionRoot is false, as removeCorrupt already could in base. The corrupt_drops_total counter no longer includes expiry, which is a telemetry-only change. The unchanged surrounding scanOnDisk code was not in the supplied excerpt. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption identified.
